system_overview: A test module for validating the correctness of reachability lemmas using the TLC model checker on small graph instances. Rather than relying solely on formal proof, this module allows testing the mathematical properties of directed-graph reachability on all possible graphs or randomly generated graphs of a given size. It serves as a practical complement to the formal proofs in the reachability proofs module.
actors_and_components: No active actors. The module defines a parametrized instantiation of the reachability proofs module that allows testing all four reachability lemmas against a set of possible successor functions (graph structures).
state_variables: No state variables. This is a constant-level testing module.
model_bounds: Two testing strategies are provided. Exhaustive: test all possible graphs over the node set (feasible for 3 nodes, producing about 6500 graphs). Random: test a specified number of randomly generated graphs, enabling testing on larger node sets (e.g., 5 nodes). Random graphs are generated by assigning each node a randomly chosen subset of nodes as its successor set.
additional_assumptions: The module uses parametrized instantiation to substitute different successor functions into the reachability proofs. The test evaluates a tuple of four Boolean values corresponding to the four reachability lemmas. Testing on small graphs is considered an effective way to catch errors in formal statements, since reachability properties that fail on large graphs almost certainly fail on graphs with 5 or fewer nodes.
